Theorem
[Infinitely many reflection-quotient manifolds] \group reflection-polyhedra Source: thurston:page-0181

1. Theorem 7.3.1There are infinitely many oriented finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifolds whose volumes are finite rational sums of $\Lambda (\theta )$ with $\theta /\pi \in \mathbb Q$.
Proof

\sketch For $\alpha ,\beta $ integral submultiples of $\pi $, reflections in the prism faces generate a discrete group. The relation $2\alpha +\beta =\pi $ leaves $(\alpha ,\beta )=(\pi /3,\pi /3)$ or $(\pi /4,\pi /2)$. Torsion-free orientation-preserving finite-index subgroups produce manifolds, and varying $n>4$ gives infinitely many cases; the volume proposition supplies the stated form.
